summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis following fundoplication was admitted for a one-day episode of severe nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She reported bloody streaks in her vomit, but examination and labs showed no active bleeding, with stable hemoglobin and prior findings of esophagitis and esophageal ulcer on recent EGD. CT scan ruled out bowel obstruction and showed stable SMA dissection and a small, unchanged adrenal nodule. She presented with anion gap metabolic acidosis and mild hypokalemia, both resolved with IV fluids and repletion. Bowel rest, IV antiemetics, and gradual restart of enteral feeds led to symptom resolution. She was discharged home on her prior medications with instructions to advance tube feeds and follow up with her PCP regarding the adrenal nodule.
